references.text: Rahab tells the spies that the inhabitants of Jericho have heard about Israel's exodus from Egypt and are seized with fear, just as Exodus 15:14 prophesied that the peoples would tremble.
The kings of the Amorites and Canaanites lost courage when they heard about Israel's crossing of the Jordan, fulfilling the prophecy that the peoples would fear Israel.
Moses describes how God will place fear and dread of Israel over all nations under heaven, paralleling the description of the peoples' fear in Exodus 15:14.
Moab was seized with terror at the sight of Israel's people, reflecting the prophecy that the peoples would tremble with fear.
The psalm uses similar language about trembling (רגזון) and birth pains (חיל) that seize the kings, paralleling Exodus 15:14.
A prophecy against Philistia (פלשת) mentions fear and trembling, linked to Exodus 15:14 which specifically names the inhabitants of Philistia.
Ezekiel describes how all creation will tremble (רגז) before the Lord's face, using the same verb found in Exodus 15:14.
Habakkuk mentions that the tent curtains in the land of Cush shook, an allusion to the peoples' fear described in Exodus 15:14.
Both verses illustrate how hostile powers are seized with terror when confronted with God's power exercised through His people.
Both verses show how news of God's judgment or salvation causes entire nations to tremble in fear.
Both verses illustrate how leaders and crowds are seized with alarm or dread when confronted with God's message.
